launches.notes:
I read both sources directly on 2026-10-12: the launch page HTML via curl, and the 230-page system card PDF, extracted as text and with figure pages rendered as images. Effort-level numbers on the launch page come from the chart data-point aria-labels in the page HTML, e.g. "Opus 5.5 · Med: 54.6% $0.80". The labels also give cost per task (USD), which I left out of the scores. Effort-level numbers in the system card were read from data labels printed on the figures.

Launch page headline table: 9 rows, columns Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.1 / Opus 5 / GPT-6 Astra / GPT-5.6 Sol. The rows are Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode v1.1 (Main), CursorBench 4.0, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench, Humanity's Last Exam (with tools only), Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, OSWorld (partial) and Chartography (with tools).

System card summary (Table 8.1.A, p.174) also has SWE-bench Pro, SWE-bench Multilingual, SWE-bench Multimodal, HLE no tools, OSWorld 2.0 strict, HealthBench Professional and AA-Briefcase v1.1. Its only non-Claude column is GPT-6 Astra.

Default setting: adaptive thinking at max effort, default sampling, averaged over 5 trials, context up to 1M tokens. Terminal-Bench 4.0 is the exception: it is reported at xhigh, its highest score (max = 64.8). Opus 5.5 ran with production safeguards on. When the safeguards intervened, cyber tasks fell back to Opus 4.8 and bio / frontier-LLM tasks to Opus 5, which Anthropic says likely lowers scores.

Discrepancies and caveats:
1. The launch table labels computer use "OSWorld 2.1"; the system card says "OSWorld 2.0" (Sept 10 2026 task files, new context-management harness). The numbers are the same (81.8 / 80.7 / 74.0 partial).
2. WANDR, Opus 5 at max: 67.2% in the launch chart, 67.1% in the card figure. Anthropic's WANDR setup (offline frozen index, Opus 4.6 judge) differs from Perplexity's and is not comparable to Perplexity's published numbers.
3. FrontierCode scores drop above medium effort. Opus 5.5's best is 54.6% at medium; the headline uses max (54.4%).
4. The Terminal-Bench 4.0 comparison mixes effort levels: GPT-6 Astra at high (as reported by OpenAI), Claude comparison models at max. Public leaderboard has Opus 5 at 51.8%.
5. Third-party runs:
   - AutomationBench was run by Zapier with no fallback, so safeguard interventions counted as failures.
   - GDPval-AA, AA-Briefcase and the Harvey LAB held-out set were run by Artificial Analysis.
   - CursorBench was run by Cursor; Opus 5.5's costs are Anthropic's estimates.
   - FrontierCode was run by Cognition.
   - FrontierSWE v2 was run by Proximal.
6. HealthBench Professional in Table 8.1.A (65.6 / 59.8 / 62.1 / 63.4) is the length-adjusted score; Opus 5.5's raw score is 77.1.
7. GMMLU (94.3) and MILU (93.1) are above 90 and likely saturated. ArXivMath with tools (96.9), BenchCAD with tools (0.962) and SWE-bench Multilingual (93.9) are also near ceiling. SWE-bench Pro (89.9) is near saturation.
8. BenchCAD Vision2Code: GPT-6 Astra (0.959) and GPT-5.6 Sol (0.706 / 0.834) are "as publicly reported by OpenAI." Astra has only one bar; I took it as with-tools from the bar shading, which is an inference. Anthropic re-ran its BenchCAD eval at 256px, so earlier Claude BenchCAD numbers (e.g. Fable 5.1 0.437 / 0.843) are superseded.
9. The ArXivMath competitors GPT-6 Astra 88.6 and Fable 5.1 87.7 come from MathArena's own setting and are not directly comparable to Anthropic's with-tools numbers.
10. Toolathlon Verified uses Anthropic's internal harness. Its numbers for Claude Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 are about 3 points above the published leaderboard (71.6 / 76.2).

Internal or non-public evals are included only for completeness:
- CoBench 2.1 and AECI (an internal index).
- The life-science internal benchmarks: morphology-to-molecule, med chem, protein design, binder design, biomedical image, Protocols.
- Cyber suites: ExploitBench, CyScenarioBench (private set), Binary Exploitation Benchmark, ExploitGym. These were run with cyber safeguards off and are reported in counts or Cap%.

Not captured as scores:
- Multi-agent results (ProgramBench teams, multi-agent DRACO, large agent teams): figures only, no single headline numbers.
- METR external testing: qualitative only.
- Safety / alignment evals: skipped as instructed.
- Customer-quoted numbers on the launch page: Deloitte "72% of known bugs", Hebbia "86.6% vs 60.3%", the internal report test "16 of 18". These are customer-internal evals, not public benchmarks.

There is no GPQA, MMMU, SWE-bench Verified, tau-bench or ARC-AGI number anywhere in either source. CyberGym was explicitly retired for saturation.

launches.notes:
Both sources were read directly on 2026-10-12. The launch page is https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5 (the /news/ URL returns 404). The system card is a 148-page PDF reached from https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5-system-card; I read section 8 (Capabilities, pp.109-144), section 2.3 (AI R&D) and section 3.2 (Cyber). The per-effort numbers in the launch page's accuracy-vs-cost charts come from the SVG aria-labels on each point (e.g. "Sonnet 5.5 · Xhigh: 61.5% $5.30"), so they are exact values, not estimates.

Headline table (8 rows, columns Sonnet 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.5 / GPT-6 Sol): Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode 1.1 (Main), CursorBench 4.0, GDPval-AA v2.1, AA-Briefcase v1.1, Humanity's Last Exam (with tools), OSWorld 2.1 (partial), Chartography (no tools).

Caveats:
- Standard configuration: unless noted, system card numbers use adaptive thinking at max effort and are averaged over 5 trials (Table 8.1.A).
- Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (66.4) is its xhigh score; at max it is 64.8.
- FrontierCode Main: the headline cell shows two numbers. 46.2 is the max-effort score and is the Table 8.1.A value; 52.1 at xhigh is Sonnet 5.5's best. Footnote 2 says max scores lower because the model ran Claude Code's code-review skill more often, causing timeouts or out-of-scope edits.
- Third parties ran several evals: FrontierCode by Cognition; CursorBench by Cursor (Sonnet 5.5 numbers came from a results table Cursor sent to Anthropic; costs are Anthropic estimates); GDPval-AA and AA-Briefcase by Artificial Analysis on a pre-release deployment with a structured-output bug (footnote 3: effect expected to be small); FrontierSWE by Proximal; AutomationBench by Zapier.
- Footnote 4: GPT-6 Sol had an image-understanding bug that OpenAI has since fixed. Its AA and Chartography scores may not reflect the fix.
- The launch charts for Terminal-Bench 4.0 and CursorBench use GPT-5.6 Sol, because GPT-6 Sol has no public score on those benchmarks. The Terminal-Bench chart's x-axis is cost per attempt.
- Not directly comparable to public leaderboards: WANDR (frozen-index search, different judge), DRACO (Opus 4.6 judge instead of the paper's Gemini 3 Pro), and ArXivMath (Anthropic's own setup differs from MathArena's).
- Some evals are internal and not publicly reproducible: the life-sciences suite, ExploitBench, CyScenarioBench, the Binary Exploitation Benchmark and AECI.
- Saturated or near-saturated: GMMLU 92.1, MILU 91.6, SWE-Bench Multilingual 90.3, ArXivMath with tools 95.2, BenchCAD with tools 0.963.
- Scores are on different scales: GDPval-AA and AA-Briefcase are Elo; BenchCAD is voxel IoU on a 0-1 scale (not percent); ExploitGym and Binary Exploitation are counts.

Not captured as exact numbers:
- FrontierCode Main/Extended charts in the card (Figs 8.4.A/B) only label effort levels for competitors (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Fable 5/5.1, Opus 5/5.5), not scores.
- The CursorBench card chart (Fig 8.8.A) shows Grok 4.7, GPT-5.6 Sol, Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 without numeric labels.
- The AutomationBench chart (Fig 8.14.6.A) has unlabeled points for Sonnet 5.5 at lower efforts and for GPT-6 Astra.
- Multi-agent ProgramBench (Fig 8.12.1.A) gives fractions of hidden tests passed only as unlabeled points (about 0.86 to 0.96).
- The ExploitBench and CyScenarioBench figures were not inspected for competitor bars beyond the numbers in the text.
- A few life-sciences competitor values (e.g. BioMysteryBench Opus 5.5 0.51, MedChem GPT-6 Astra 0.57) come from bar labels in Fig 8.17.A rounded to two decimals; the text gives exact Sonnet 5.5 values.

Skipped: pure safety and alignment evaluations (harmful requests, BBQ, MASK, hallucination, SHADE-Arena, LinuxArena, prompt injection), per the task.

SWE-Bench Pro (81.3), SWE-Bench Multilingual (90.3) and SWE-Bench Multimodal (54.3) appear only in the system card, not in the launch headline table. The card does not state their harness; the 5-trial average comes from the card text and the effort from the standard configuration.

launches.notes:
Sources were read on 2026-10-12. Launch page: https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1 (the /news/... and /claude-fable-5-1 URLs return 404). The system card PDF is 212 pages. Its capabilities section is Section 8 (pp.166-205) and its cyber section is Section 3.3.

Headline table on the launch page has nine rows, all marked launch_page_headline: TB-Science 0.1, Terminal-Bench 4.0 (55.8, with Mythos 5.1 at 60.9 in the same cell), GDPval-AA v2, OSWorld 2.0 partial and strict, HLE no tools and with tools, AutomationBench, CursorBench 3.2.0. The columns are Fable 5.1 / Fable 5 / Opus 5 / GPT-5.6 Sol. The launch page also has effort-sweep charts for TB-Science, TB 4.0, HLE and CursorBench. I took exact per-effort values from the chart data embedded in the HTML.

Default config: unless noted, the card uses adaptive thinking at max effort, default sampling, an average of 5 trials, and at most 1M context. Fable 5.1 was evaluated with production safeguards on, so tasks the safeguards blocked scored 0 on OSWorld/AutomationBench, and other blocked tasks fell back to Opus 4.8 (cyber) or Opus 5 (bio). This likely lowers Fable 5.1's scores somewhat. The TB 4.0 gap between Fable 5.1 (55.8) and Mythos 5.1 (60.9) comes from safeguard interventions; the weights are identical.

Rounding: the card's summary table rounds TB 4.0 to 56% (61%), with Fable 5 at 42% (45%) and Opus 5 at 52%; the text gives 55.8/60.9/42.0/52.3. Public leaderboard values the card cites: TB 4.0 Opus 5 51.8 and Fable 5 44.5; TB-Science Opus 5 30.0 and Fable 5 21.4.

Some sections only evaluated Mythos 5.1, not Fable 5.1. These are: all cyber evals (ExploitBench, OSS-Fuzz, Firefox 147, ExploitGym, run with safeguards off), ArXivMath, AA-Omniscience, and the life-sciences evals. The card says Fable 5.1's cyber scores would roughly match Opus 4.8's because its classifiers fire on those tasks, so no Fable 5.1 cyber scores are reported. Many of the life-sciences evals are internal or private.

Nonstandard harnesses or versions:
- CritPT-Corrected is Anthropic's own corrected version (31 of 71 problems fixed).
- DRACO uses an Opus 4.6 judge, and GDP.pdf uses an Opus 4.7 judge, so neither is comparable to the original papers.
- ProgramBench uses a 166-task subset.
- BenchCAD uses a 1,000-file subset.
- OSWorld 2.0 uses the August 2026 task release, which is not comparable to earlier OSWorld 2.0 numbers.
- OfficeQA is very sensitive to harness choice; Databricks' own image-based run gives Fable 5 57.9 on Pro.
- FrontierCode is best at medium effort. Max-effort values appear only as chart points without labels; on the Extended chart Fable 5.1 max is about 62, but I did not record it because it is not printed.
- FrontierSWE v2 and BenchCAD use a 0-1 scale (kept native, not converted to %).
- GMMLU (94.0) and MILU (93.0) are above 90 and likely saturated. So is ARC-AGI-1 (97.5); ARC-AGI-2 is at 90.0.

Skipped:
- Internal or safety-only metrics: CoBench (no number in text), AECI 161.98 (internal Epoch-style index for Mythos 5.1), METR qualitative findings, SHADE-Arena, MASK, harmlessness and prompt-injection evals.
- Multi-agent ProgramBench, which is reported only as curves with no single number.
- Customer quotes on the launch page, which are partner claims: Browserbase 82% vs Opus 5 74% vs Fable 5 57% on its own browser-agent benchmark; Crosby RedlineBench 57.0 vs 47.9; Samaya FrontierFinance 55.9% vs 49.2%.

Competitor numbers come from Anthropic's tables, and some are re-runs by Anthropic. The card's GPT-5.6 Sol figures are drawn from public leaderboards or OpenAI.

launches.notes:
Checked 2026-10-12 against the launch page (HTML plus its embedded data payload) and the 144-page system card PDF (text extraction, with figure pages rendered as images and read).

1) Launch-page headline table (benchmarkGrid). Columns: Haiku 5.5, Haiku 4.5, GPT-6 Luna, and Sonnet 5.5 (Sonnet is shaded "For reference"). Eight rows: GDPval-AA v2.1, AA-Briefcase v1.1, OSWorld 2.1 offline subset, HLE no tools, HLE with tools, Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode 1.1 (Main), Chartography no tools. Every Haiku 5.5 headline number is at max effort: the effort-sweep chart points for Max match the table, and system card Table 8.1.A says the standard configuration is "adaptive thinking at max effort ... averaged over five trials".

2) FrontierCode discrepancy. On the launch page, Sonnet 5.5 is shown at 52.1% and labeled "Xhigh". In the system card table, Sonnet 5.5 is 46.2 at max and 52.1 at xhigh; Haiku 5.5 is 46.4 at max and 45.8 at xhigh. The card notes that Cognition's public leaderboard shows each model at its best effort, so its numbers can differ from the card's.

3) Where the GPT-6 Luna numbers come from. OSWorld: run by Anthropic through the OpenAI API with OpenAI's own compaction. Terminal-Bench 4.0: 16.4 is from the public leaderboard (Codex CLI, max); the card says OpenAI has not reported its own TB 4.0 score for Luna. Chartography: 29.1 is as reported by Surge AI. GDPval-AA and AA-Briefcase: run by Artificial Analysis. HealthBench, HealthBench Professional and PhysicianBench: Anthropic's own runs, not OpenAI's published figures. The 65.5% HealthBench Professional value for Luna appears only in Figure 8.11.1.A; Table 8.1.A shows "–".

4) Effort sweeps. The launch-page sweep values come from the page's embedded chart CSV, so they are exact. Sweeps that appear only in system card figures, with the printed labels I read:

launches.notes:
ACCESS: openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra/ returns 403 to normal browsers, curl, WebFetch and Googlebot user agents, and archive.org and r.jina.ai are blocked. The page did return in full with User-Agent "Slackbot-LinkExpanding 1.0 (+https://api.slack.com/robots)". Everything in this report comes from that HTML (the comparison table, chart captions, footnotes, and the embedded Vega chart data that carries per-effort points) plus the HTML system card at deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-6-astra. The system card PDF downloaded, but no PDF renderer is installed, so it was not read. Figure images in the system card were read directly as PNGs.

HEADLINE: The launch page has one large comparison table at the bottom, with sections Computer Use, Professional, Coding, Academic, Science and Health, Cybersecurity, Alignment, Long Context and Abstract reasoning. Its columns are GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash. Every row of that table is marked launch_page_headline. The hero chart at the top of the page has tabs for only five benchmarks: Terminal-Bench Science 0.1, ARC-AGI-3, FrontierMath Tier 4 (v2), Terminal-Bench 4.0 and AutomationBench. Global setting stated on the page: "Evaluation scores are the maximum at any effort." GPT evaluations were run in OpenAI's research environment or API. The table reports no SWE-bench (Verified, Pro or Multilingual), no MMMU and no HLE without tools.

EFFORT AT MAX (from chart data):
- At max: Agents' Last Exam, OSWorld, AutomationBench, Design Tasks, GPQA, ExploitGym, SRE-Bench, MLE-Bench Revised.
- At xhigh: ScreenSpot-Pro, DeepSWE, GeneBench Pro.
- At high: Terminal-Bench 4.0 (57.88; xhigh 57.58, max 56.67).
- Tied: FrontierMath 97.6 at medium/high/xhigh/max. AA Coding Agent Index 67.0 at xhigh and max.
- Not labeled in the data: BenchCAD, BrowseComp, OpenScore, FrontierCode, LifeSciBench, MedChemBench, HealthBench Professional.

CODE MODE: The chart data labels Astra's series "Code" (code_mode=true) and competitors' series "Non-code" on FrontierMath, DeepSWE, AA Coding Agent Index, HealthBench Professional and TB-Science. So Astra may have had a code tool that the competitors did not. This is an inference from the field names; the page text does not explain it.

COMPETITOR CAVEATS:
- Claude ScreenSpot-Pro and ExploitGym numbers are Mythos (Fable with fewer safeguards), per footnote 17.
- Claude BenchCAD numbers use a modified eval from the Fable 5.1 system card (footnote 5).
- Claude HealthBench Professional scores were run by OpenAI with a GPT-5.4 grader (footnote 11).
- Claude OSWorld scores were reproduced on the official leaderboard (footnote 3).
- Fable 5.1 FrontierCode Main is printed as 50.9 here. A local note says Anthropic's own page gives 50.3; I did not re-check that here.

INCONSISTENCIES:
1. HealthBench Professional is 63.4 on the launch page but 64.7 length-adjusted in system card Table 6 (68.2 unadjusted). GPT-5.6 Sol is 60.5 in both.
2. ExploitBench Internal Port (June–Aug 2026) is 39.0% on the launch page. The system card's GPT-6 Sol appendix says "GPT-6 Astra's 31.5%". System card Figure 47 has two Astra lines: about 39% for "V8 with additional API attack-surface enabled" and about 31.5% for "V8 with reduced API attack-surface". So the two numbers are probably different configurations, not a correction. These two values were read from the chart image, so treat them as approximate.
3. The launch intro rounds FrontierMath Tier 4 to "98%"; the table says 97.6%.

NOT RECORDED AS SCORES (chart images without number labels; rough readings only): KernelGen 1P about 67% rubric score (Sol about 61%). NanoGPT about 23.5% mean reward (Sol about 16.5%; best human 72.38%). PostTrainBench Lite about 77% mean reward (Sol about 53%). The bio/chem Preparedness evals (Multimodal Troubleshooting Virology, ProtocolQA, Tacit Knowledge, TroubleshootingBench and others) were skipped; their numbers are only in figures and the text has no numeric values. The hallucination chart (Figure 6) has no text numbers.

OTHER LAUNCH-PAGE TEXT CLAIMS:
- OSWorld 2.0 latency simulation: Astra 72.6% at about 40 minutes per task vs GPT-5.6 Sol 65.7% at about 75 minutes.
- Mind2Web: 1.9x faster task completion (no score given).
- Hugging Face-incident scope eval: 0% for Astra vs 48% for GPT-5.6 Sol.
- Internal Database Migration at a lower-cost setting: 63.4%.

SYSTEM CARD SUPPLEMENTS:
- The appendix gives GPT-6 Sol 81.7% and Luna 43.4% on ExploitBench, and Sol 66.3% and Luna 34.2% on SEC-Bench Pro, compared with Astra 85.4%.
- Retired evals: internal CTF and CVE-Bench (saturated) and VulnLMP. Monorepo-Bench and OPQA were dropped from the self-improvement suite.
- Expert-led assessments ran at Codex Ultra reasoning effort with up to 64 subagents. They are qualitative, with no scores.

Safety and alignment rows from the headline table are included with category=safety so they can be filtered out. The AA Coding Agent Index row is v1.4; the current AA index is v1.5, so the numbers are not comparable.

I could not read the launch page directly. https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-sol/ returned HTTP 403 (a Cloudflare challenge) to curl, WebFetch and the r.jina.ai reader proxy, and web.archive.org was unreachable. The local note from 2026-10-10 hit the same 403. So every launch-page number above comes from secondary sources that reproduce OpenAI's chart data, not from openai.com itself.
- I used the AlphaCorp AI article as source_url because it is the only one with the full five-effort tables.
- Where sources overlap, the numbers agree exactly. OrcaRouter matches all of DeepSWE, the max and medium points of OSWorld and AutomationBench, the GDP.pdf max values, the Terminal-Bench Science endpoints and the factuality values. Emergent matches the whole DeepSWE table for all three OpenAI models.
- The numbers also fit the relative claims that Layer3 Labs and DataCamp quote from the post: DeepSWE +6.4 pts over GPT-6 Sol's best (75.2 vs 68.8); OSWorld max +7 over GPT-6 Sol and within 2.1 of Astra (71.4 vs 64.4 / 73.5); AutomationBench medium +2.2 over Opus 5.5 and +4.8 over GPT-6 Sol (31.7 vs 29.5 / 26.9); Terminal-Bench Science max more than double GPT-6 Sol (57.0 vs 27.6); Astra at 68.1; low-effort factual errors 11.4% to 7.7%.
- Treat the launch numbers as vendor-reported, as relayed by secondary sources, until the OpenAI page can be opened in a browser.

Launch page contents: the secondary sources describe five capability charts plotting score against cost per task at reasoning effort low, medium (default), high, xhigh and max. They are DeepSWE v1.1 (113 tasks across 91 repos), GDP.pdf, AutomationBench 1.0.6 (47 tools), OSWorld 2.0 (offline set v2026.08.08, 108 workflows, partial reward, so 71.4% does not mean 71.4% of tasks completed) and Terminal-Bench Science 0.1. I marked these five as launch_page_headline. A sixth chart is the factuality error rate; I marked it launch_page_other. The page has no single headline table.
- Several secondary sources say the post contains no SWE-bench Pro, HLE, GPQA, ARC-AGI, Terminal-Bench 4.0 or MMLU-type numbers. OpenAI did not self-report Terminal-Bench 4.0 for GPT-6.1 Sol.
- Claude numbers in these charts are what OpenAI printed, not what Anthropic reported. Opus 5.5 is labelled "with fallbacks", and OpenAI says the Fable 5.1 AutomationBench cost leaves out fallbacks, which happened on about 40% of tasks.
- Pick of main scores (my judgement, not an OpenAI statement): DeepSWE at max is 71.9, but the best is 75.2 at high. GDP.pdf at max is 31.0, best 32.0 at high. Terminal-Bench Science at max is 57.0. OSWorld at max is 71.4. AutomationBench at max is 36.1.

System card: I downloaded the 45-page PDF from the cdn.openai.com URL and read all of it. I also checked the deploymentsafety.openai.com PDF (48 pages) and the HTML hub page; their text matches apart from page and table numbering.
- The PDF says comparison values for older models "may reflect later versions of those models, and may vary from the values published at launch."
- Capability-type sections: HealthBench (Table 7), MentalHealthBench (Figure 4 table), bio High/Critical evals, cyber (ExploitBench, ExploitBench Internal Port, SEC-Bench Pro, ExploitGym) and AI self-improvement (Internal Research Debugging, KernelGen 1P).
- I read the KernelGen 1P values and some competitor points (GPT-5.6 Sol 78.5 and GPT-6 Luna 43.4 on ExploitBench; GPT-6 Luna 34.2 on SEC-Bench Pro and 11.6 on ExploitGym) from the bar or line labels in rendered figures, not from text.
- The hallucination chart (Figure 5: any-hallucination rate vs latency) has no printed values, so I did not record it.
- I left out safety and alignment items: production challenging prompts, jailbreaks, prompt injection 99.99%, dynamic mental-health simulations, auto-review, warnings 23.5%, honeypot, coding deception 1.50%, broken search tool 2.08%, Codex traffic simulation, CoT controllability and monitor evasion.
- ExploitBench and ExploitGym may be inflated by contamination, per OpenAI.
- The cyber and research-debugging evals are internal or Preparedness evals and not standard public leaderboards. HealthBench Consensus is saturated (above 95 for every model).

Independent numbers seen in search results, not verified and not part of this OpenAI extraction:
- Artificial Analysis: Intelligence Index 52 at max (GPT-6 Sol 48); Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 30.8 / 48.0 / 54.0 / 56.1 for low / medium / xhigh / max; HLE at 47.4 / 49.9 / 52.6.
- Vals AI: Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 55.05%.
- Terminal-Bench 4.0 public leaderboard (from the local note): 58.2%.

GPT-6 Sol (released 2026-09-22) is now superseded by GPT-6.1 Sol at the same $2 / $10 per million token price (cached input goes from $0.20 to $0.10). Its scores appear above as competitor columns. launches.notes:
GPT-5.6 Terra launched to general availability on 2026-07-09. OpenAI's RSS feed lists 'GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition' at openai.com/index/gpt-5-6 on that date. Before that, from 2026-06-26, there was a limited preview of Sol only. Secondary sources say Terra's numbers were first published at GA.

1) The launch page could not be read. openai.com/index/gpt-5-6/ returns HTTP 403 to curl (including a Googlebot user agent) and to WebFetch. Wayback and archive.ph are blocked, and r.jina.ai rejected the request because of IP reputation. So every number tagged launch_page_headline comes from a secondary reproduction of OpenAI's launch eval tables, not from the OpenAI page itself:
- Kingy.ai (kingy.ai/blog/gpt-5-6-sol-terra-luna-benchmarks-specs/; the sources entry mislabels its title, but its note gives this URL) reproduces the tables row by row with all competitor columns, in groups: professional, coding, computer use, cyber, science, reasoning, and tool/long-context.
- BenchLM marks the same Terra values as 'Provider exact OpenAI: GPT-5.6'.
- PromptHQ and Vellum match on the rows they include.

2) Cross-checks against the first-party system card:
- The CTF bar chart has exact labels (Sol 96.67, Terra 91.84, GPT-5.5 88.06, Luna 85.19). These match Kingy's 96.7 / 91.8 / 88.1 / 85.2.
- The HealthBench Professional table matches exactly (Sol 60.5, Terra 57.7, Luna 55.7).
- The tops of the system card curves for SEC-Bench Pro (~57.7), ExploitBench (~53) and ExploitGym at the 6h cap (~23) match the reproduced launch values.
These matches support the reproduction's accuracy, but I could not verify any row directly against the launch page.

3) Which rows form the 'headline' table versus later sections or appendix tables is not verified. I tagged every Kingy-reproduced row as launch_page_headline. Secondary sources say OpenAI 'led with' Terminal-Bench, Agents' Last Exam, BrowseComp, OSWorld and the AA Coding Agent Index.

4) The reasoning-effort setting for the launch table is not stated in any source I read. OpenAI says it plots curves across effort levels. Artificial Analysis says Terra (max) scores 55 on Intelligence Index v4.1 and 77 on the Coding Agent Index, which matches the launch-table values 55 and 77.4. This suggests the table uses max effort, but that is an inference.

5) The MMMU-Pro rows (80.7 no tools, 82.0 with Python) come only from aggregators that attribute them to OpenAI GPT-5.6 (BenchLM, PromptHQ). Kingy's tables do not include them, so I tagged them launch_page_other. The Sol 83.0 value comes only from a search-result snippet.

6) A Miraheze wiki says OpenAI's comparison also had FrontierCode 1.1 and 'Graphwalks BFS >128K' rows, and that GPT-5.5 beat Terra on FrontierCode 1.1 and MMMU-Pro. I could not find OpenAI's FrontierCode number for Terra. BenchLM's 'FrontierCode 1.1 Extended 55.8%' is attributed to Cognition/Devin, not OpenAI, so I excluded it. The same wiki gives GPQA as 92.5, which conflicts with 92.9 everywhere else; treat the wiki as unreliable.

7) Possible errors in the reproduction:
- Kingy lists Luna at 41.3% in both MRCR rows, which may be a transcription error.
- Vellum gives Claude Fable 5 Terminal-Bench 2.1 as 86.0 (Anthropic self-report). OpenAI's table, via Kingy, shows 83.1.
- An older Lushbinary article gives different Terminal-Bench numbers (Terra 84.3), possibly from a pre-GA chart.
- A search summary claimed Terra's Terminal-Bench 2.1 moved from 82.5 to 87.4 between preview and GA. I did not find this claim on any page I opened, so it is unverified.

8) System card (deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-6, PDF dated 2026-07-09, change log Aug 3 and Aug 19):
- Exact Terra numbers appear for CTF (91.84%) and the HealthBench family (Professional 57.7, base 57.0, Hard 32.7, Consensus 95.1; the length-adjusted score is the main one, with unadjusted scores given in settings).
- CVE-Bench, Internal Research Debugging, KernelGen 1P v3, NanoGPT, PostTrainBench Lite and MLE-Bench Revised appear only as unlabeled curves. Their values here are approximate chart readings at the highest-effort point. Do not treat them as exact. I omitted MLE-Bench Revised because its y-axis has only a 50% tick (Terra's top is roughly in the 70s, too uncertain to read).
- Bio evals (TroubleshootingBench, ProtocolQA, etc.) and the SecureBio, Irregular, UK AISI and METR external evals cover Sol only, or have no labeled Terra values.
- Safety and robustness evals that include Terra (disallowed content, vision safety, prompt injection: GPT-Red direct 0.061% / indirect 3.32% attack success, mental-health dynamic evals, data-destructive actions, user confirmations) are omitted as non-capability evals.

9) Third-party scores mentioned by the aggregators are not OpenAI-reported: Vals AI Terminal-Bench 2.1 77.5%, ARC Prize ARC-AGI-2 83.9% and ARC-AGI-1 96.5% (Terra max), Terminal-Bench 3.0 20.8%, CursorBench. They can be used as external cross-references.

10) Pricing context: launch price was $2.50/$15 per 1M tokens, cut to $2/$12 on 2026-07-30. The OpenAI API docs describe Terra as roughly the 'mini' tier and list reasoning efforts none through max.

Two independent transcriptions agree on every Luna value: kingy.ai, which gives full low/medium/high/xhigh/max scores and $/task, and aicatchup.com. Tosea.ai and VentureBeat confirm the headline values (DeepSWE 66.6%, AutomationBench 20.7%, max effort). source_url points to the official page for referencing, but a reviewer should open it in a real browser to confirm before publishing.
2) The launch page has no conventional table. It shows score-vs-cost-per-task charts, one point per reasoning effort, for six evals: AutomationBench 1.0.6, Agents' Last Exam V1, FrontierCode 1.1 Main, DeepSWE v1.1, OSWorld 2.0 offline, and an internal factuality error rate. I treated all six as 'launch_page_headline'. The suggested primary score is Luna at max effort, its best point everywhere: DeepSWE 66.6, FrontierCode Main 42.4, OSWorld 2.0 offline 52.7, ALE 50.9, AutomationBench 20.7, factual error 7.6. Lower efforts are reference values only. OpenAI's text says scores were run 'in our research environment or via our API' and competitor scores were 'taken from publicly available reports'. The harness is not stated for any chart.
3) Competitor values printed in the charts come from the kingy.ai transcription. One oddity: kingy lists GPT-5.6 Luna OSWorld at 52.7% ($0.49), identical to GPT-6 Luna, which may be a transcription error. No Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini or Grok appear in OpenAI's charts.
4) Not reported by OpenAI for Luna: Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench Pro, HLE, GPQA, ARC-AGI, MMMU and similar. Cross-references from other sources (not official OpenAI numbers, not included above): Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 page (2026-10-07) prints GPT-6 Luna at Terminal-Bench 4.0 16.4% and FrontierCode 1.1 Main 42.4%, per local note research/frontier-coding-benchmarks/notes/01-launch-posts.md (not re-verified this session). Artificial Analysis, as relayed by tosea.ai, reports Luna (max): Intelligence Index 37 (v4.3), Coding Agent Index v1.5 41, Terminal-Bench 4.0 13%, SWE-Atlas-QnA 44%, DeepSWE v1.1 64% (AA's own run), AutomationBench-AA 53%, AA-Omniscience hallucination rate 77%, and GDPval-AA v2.1 1367 Elo per codersera.
5) System card: Luna results are in the GPT-6 Astra System Card, Section 11 appendix, added 2026-09-22 (HTML read directly; figures 79-85 read as images). The ExploitGym and SEC-Bench Pro chart curves have no effort labels; reported values are the curve maxima. Sandbox Bench is stored as 4.5% (1/22). Skipped as pure safety evals: refusals, jailbreak/prompt-injection defender rates, U18, mental health, alignment evals (coding deception 2.8% vs 9.5% for GPT-5.6 Luna, broken search tool 30.2%, and others), and bio refusal tables. The hallucination 'cases flagged by users' figure (Figure 60) was downloaded but not transcribed; the launch-page factuality chart covers the same internal eval. Luna was omitted from CoT monitorability results and from Critical-threshold bio testing.
6) A separate 'GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna: October 2026 update' card exists (deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-6-october, 2026-10-07). It covers a later October snapshot used in ChatGPT and was not part of the launch, so it was not extracted.

coverage.notes:
Retrieved 2026-10-12. Every vendor number above was read on the vendor's own page or PDF. Charts drawn as images (Mistral, Meta scorecard) were downloaded and read visually. Main findings:
(1) The benchmarks reported most widely across these 5 vendors plus the frontier labs are: DeepSWE v1.1 (all 5), Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Argon, 3.8 Flash, Grok, Mistral; Meta still reports TB 2.1, which is saturated at ~89), Harvey LAB and Vals Finance Agent v2 (Google x2, Grok, Mistral), AutomationBench (Argon, Meta, Mistral-AA), GDPval-AA / AA-Briefcase (3.8 Flash, Meta, Grok, Mistral), OSWorld 2.0 partial (Argon, 3.8 Flash, Meta), SWE-Atlas QnA (Meta, Mistral, 3.8 Flash guide), FrontierSWE v2, CursorBench 4.0, HLE-Verified/HLE, LVBench, LABBench2, CWE-bench, GraphWalks/MRCR. SWE-bench Verified, TB 2.1 and SWE-Bench Pro V2 (Scale board ~99%) look saturated.
(2) Source caveats. Argon's DeepSWE (77.9), Argon's TB 4.0 (57.4) and Muse's DeepSWE (75.4) are self-run. None of the three appears on the official boards (Datacurve as of 9-22, tbench as of 10-06). Mistral's coding numbers were run privately by Artificial Analysis, not by Mistral. Mistral states settings for almost none of its numbers. Google's pages give no per-row effort level (the methodology says highest thinking, pass@1).
(3) Conflicts found:
- Gemini 3.8 Flash TB 2.1: model card 89.4 vs Vertex developer guide 90.8.
- Grok 4.7 TB 4.0: launch page and official board 37.6 vs model card 38.0.
- Grok 4.7 EEBench: launch page 64.0 vs card 66.0.
- Muse Spark 1.3: third-party blogs (DataCamp) give AutomationBench 49.4 and DeepSearchQA 89.4; the official scorecard says 49.6 and 90.3.
- Muse Spark 1.3 headline scores are at max effort, but the shipping/leaderboard runs are xhigh (TB 4.0 board 14.55; Vals 10.61 vs Max 24.75).
(4) Not verified from primary sources: the Zapier AutomationBench board (search summary only); the ARC-AGI-3 and OSWorld 2.0 official boards (both load dynamically); AA's Mistral score of 38 (search snippet); Gemini 3.8 Flash's own eval-methodology page. coverage.notes:
The vendor score tables for all 10 Chinese models were found and read; every number above comes from a source opened in this session. Read on 2026-10-12.

Where the numbers came from:
- Hugging Face model cards: Kimi K3, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL; MiMo also via its tech report PDF.
- GLM-5.3-Flash: only a bar-chart image on the HF card. I read the values off the image.
- Qwen3.8-Max-0902: only a table image in the official @Alibaba_Qwen X post. The QwenCloud model page has no numbers.
- Ling 3.1 Flash: only a bar-chart image in the official @AntLingAGI X post. No settings are given except that HealthBench Professional was run in Ant's AQ app.
- Step 5 Preview: the official model page is rendered by JavaScript. I took the full table (6 models x about 40 rows) from the page's JS bundle at https://www.stepfun.com/assets/index-Cp9oF7Fw.js.
- X images were fetched through the api.fxtwitter.com mirror. The image URLs are the original pbs.twimg.com files.

Model names:
- 'DeepSeek V4.1' on Artificial Analysis (AA) is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. No non-Flash V4.1 exists.
- Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B is the open-weight form of the original Qwen3.8-Max (2026-08-03). Its HF table column is labelled 'Qwen3.8-Max'.

Most widely reported benchmarks across the 10 vendor tables (count of tables):
- DeepSWE v1.1: 9
- AutomationBench: 9, but in three different versions (600-task public subset, v1.0.6 with PR #13, v1.0.6 with PR #16, plus AA's AutomationBench-AA)
- Agents' Last Exam (ALE-CLI): 8
- Terminal-Bench 2.1: 7, saturated at 84-91
- Toolathlon-Verified: 7
- GDPval-AA v2/v2.1 (Elo): 6
- HLE with tools: 6
- ProgramBench: 6, with three different metrics (Almost-Solved / Almost@1, pass rate, fully solved on Vals)
- JobBench: 6
- HLE without tools: 5
- NL2Repo-Bench: 5
- CyberGym: 5
- GPQA Diamond: 5, saturated at 90-96
- Terminal-Bench 4.0: 4, but it is AA's index component and has the TB official and Vals boards
- Terminal-Bench 3.0: 3
- FrontierSWE: 4
- SWE-Marathon: 4
- MLS-Bench-Lite: 4
- SWE-Atlas QnA: 3
- MMMU-Pro, BabyVision, tau3-Banking: 3 each
- OSWorld-Verified, MCP-Atlas, BrowseComp, SciCode, PostTrainBench, SkillsBench, Finance Agent v2, DRACO, APEX-Agents, OfficeQA Pro, SEC-Bench Pro, ExploitGym/ExploitBench: 2-3 each

Saturated or near-saturated:
- TB 2.1 (84-91)
- GPQA Diamond (90-96)
- LiveCodeBench v6 (about 92)
- SWE-bench Pro public v2 on Scale (top 99.4, GLM-5.3 95.6)
- MCPMark-Verified (Kimi 94.5)
- PaperBench (Qwen 93)
- OmniDocBench, MathVision, Video-MME (90+)
- CyberGym (MiMo 94)

Settings that make the same benchmark name incomparable:
- FrontierSWE: vendor 'dominance score' (73-81) vs Proximal mean@5 (GLM-5.3 30.2, Kimi K3 25.9).
- ProgramBench: Almost-Solved (Qwen/GLM/DeepSeek, about 20-28) vs pass rate (Kimi 77.8, Step 80.5) vs fully solved (Vals, at most 18.5).
- SWE-bench Pro: Qwen re-runs a 'refined' task set.
- HLE with tools: Step and GLM are on the text-only subset per StepFun's footnote; GLM's own card says full set for Flash.
- Harness changes results a lot. DeepSeek DeepSWE ranges 65.5-74.2 across 8 harnesses. Kimi uses its own Kimi Code harness. TB 4.0 for DeepSeek: 31.2 (DeepSeek's own harness), 26.8 (AA), 19.7 (Vals, mini-SWE-agent).
- Effort: Step was run at High while the models it compares against were at Max.
- AA-derived rows (GDPval-AA, CritPt, AA-LCR, SciCode, Briefcase) cited in vendor tables are snapshots and have since moved. For example, GLM-5.3 GDPval was 1769 on its card and is 1651 on AA now.

Third-party boards that cover the frontier 2026 models (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon) together with these Chinese models: AA (all of them), Vals, LMArena, APEX-Agents, FrontierSWE, and the TB 4.0 official board (no Argon or Kimi). Scale SEAL boards mostly show frontier and US models in their top rows.

Unverified or gaps:
- MiMo's card gives no harness or effort for its own scores.
- Ling's chart has no settings.
- The DeepSWE server snapshot looks stale. It lacks Opus 5.5, Argon and V4.1; an earlier local note says Argon is 77.9 there, which I did not re-check.
- ARC-AGI, HLE (lastexam.ai), ALE and SWE-Marathon boards render client-side, so no scores were extracted.
- Kimi blog/tech report, DeepSeek tech report, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next blog and MiMo blog were not read; the HF cards were used instead.
- The Arena text-board ranks were parsed from mixed page JSON and may not match the default view.

Downloads used are under source-downloads/dl/ (hf/, misc/, aa/, boards/, glm/, mimo-report/). Nineteen board HTML files were briefly written into the worktree root by mistake; I moved them to source-downloads/dl/boards, so the worktree is clean.
